status: Authored and internally reviewed; source, content, audio, focused browser and production offline gates passed. Native review pending.
method: Japan Foundation teacher guidance and role-language scholarship anchor recognition of fictional cues. Teacher/publisher pages cross-check formations. No official JLPT tag for character speech, no demographic identification from endings, and no native listening certification. Kinsui's lecture was readable in earlier research; repeat PDF fetch timed out, so the accessibility limitation is recorded.

points.form: Bundles of role-language cues; actor versus character
points.location: Japan Foundation, Keiko Kawashima, character expressions and variation; Kinsui lecture on role language; JF character line-up.
points.formation: Pronouns, address forms and endings combine into stylised cues. The same message can be expressed with different bundles. An actual performer and the fictional role are separate.
points.teachingChoice: Original script with explicit cast assignment. Speaker tasks refer to the actual labelled scene line, never a presumed demographic voice. Regional varieties are not incorrect Japanese.

points.location: Maggie Sensei, suffix sections for ぜ/ぞ; JF familiar character-expression examples.
points.formation: Plain verbs/i-adjectives attach the emphatic ending directly; nouns/na-adjectives keep だ. Volitional + ぜ can invite an action. Function depends on sentence and situation.
points.teachingChoice: Recognise labelled script emphasis, intention and warning. Avoid categorical male/villain identification or an instruction to use these in every conversation.

points.formation: Taught script pattern V/i-adjective + わ, N/na-adjective + だわ. Wondering plain phrase + かしら without final noun/na-adjective だ.
points.teachingChoice: Describe feminine-marked tendencies contextually. Maggie explicitly acknowledges different regional/intonational わ uses by men. Recognise doubt, not certainty; retain かな as the earlier neutral wondering bridge. Do not reproduce Wasabi's recommendation to choose forms solely by the learner's gender. Audio checks do not verify sociolinguistic intonation.

levels: Lower-level retrieval, not an anime-exclusive or newly N3-only form
points.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + のだ/んだ; affirmative noun/na-adjective + なのだ/なんだ; negatives attach directly. Polite のです/んです.
points.teachingChoice: Use context-linked explanation/interpretation without equating an emphatic statement with truth. Bunpro's claim that only の is correct is not adopted: common spoken ん is accepted, consistent with Wasabi's parallel conjugations.

points.form: Older copulas じゃ/でござる
points.formation: In the labelled script, noun/na-adjective + じゃ represents だ; explanatory V/i-adjective + のじゃ represents のだ. Taught samurai noun phrase + でござる corresponds to a copular statement, not a generic verb suffix.
points.teachingChoice: Recognition only; explicit older fictional roles. じゃ has real dialect uses too, so it does not certify the actual speaker's age. Distinguish じゃ from じゃん/じゃない. Do not present でござる as the current workplace keigo model.

remaining: Native sentence/listening review. Two lessons, 32 new pairs, five notes, two ten-line scenes, 214-character message, 18 tasks.
